research_run.user_request: Research Snowflake Inc, NYSE: SNOW, produce an innovation dashboard using Desert Rose, and separate Instagram carousel assets.
research_run.time_horizon: Five-year evidence, mainly fiscal 2022 through fiscal 2026 for company metrics and calendar 2021-2025 for publications and patents.

focus_technologies: AI Data Cloud architecture for multi-cloud data warehousing, sharing, governance, and applications
Snowpark, Snowpark Container Services, Cortex AI, Snowflake Intelligence, Cortex Code, and Project SnowWork
Apache Iceberg interoperability and Polaris Catalog for open lakehouse architecture

source_availability.note: FY2026 10-K, prior 10-Ks, submissions, and SEC companyfacts were accessible with declared user agent.
OpenAlex reproducible query counts were used as field-level proxies for cloud data warehousing/lakehouse and enterprise AI/data-cloud research.

iDIYAS provided assignee patent counts by grant year and filing year; PubChem, USPTO.report, and Google/Justia indexed pages provided representative patent-family evidence. Counts are treated as patent grants/documents, not clean global patent-family counts.
Snowflake official press releases, product blogs, and docs were available for Arctic, Polaris, Cortex AI, Snowflake Intelligence, Cortex Code, and Project SnowWork.

search_log.selection_reason: Primary company disclosure and audited financial/operating metrics.

search_log.query: OpenAlex cloud data warehouse query optimization lakehouse Apache Iceberg 2021-2025
search_log.selection_reason: Reproducible field-level publication trend for core data-platform science.

search_log.query: OpenAlex enterprise AI data cloud semantic layer text to SQL 2021-2025
search_log.selection_reason: Reproducible field-level publication trend for enterprise AI/data-cloud application science.
Provided usable Snowflake patent-count series by year.

exclusions.candidate_source_or_metric: Unverified market-share estimates and analyst commentary
exclusions.reason: Not primary enough for deterministic scoring.

exclusions.candidate_source_or_metric: Peer-relative score against Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, or Datadog
exclusions.reason: Single-company mode; no peer benchmark was requested or built.

exclusions.candidate_source_or_metric: Google Patents exact annual query counts
exclusions.reason: Automated repeated queries were unreliable in this environment; iDIYAS and representative patent records were used instead.

judgment_calls.decision: Scored Snowflake as a cloud data-platform and enterprise AI infrastructure innovator, not as a frontier foundation-model company.
judgment_calls.rationale: Snowflake's strongest innovation evidence is governed data/AI platform industrialization and adoption; Arctic is strategically relevant but not the entire thesis.
judgment_calls.impact: Raised Industrialization and Adoption while avoiding over-crediting model science.

judgment_calls.decision: Used patent grants by calendar year as the main trend and noted filing-year lag separately.
judgment_calls.rationale: Grant counts are observable but not identical to patent-family creation. Filing-year counts for 2024-2025 are highly lagged.
judgment_calls.impact: Held IP below exceptional despite a large absolute patent base.

judgment_calls.decision: Used FY2026 10-K as latest reported annual period and included official 2026 AI announcements as product pipeline evidence.
judgment_calls.rationale: As of 2026-05-04, FY2026 was the latest annual filing and Q1 FY2027 results were not yet available.
judgment_calls.impact: Dashboard freshness is FY2026 with April 2026 product updates.

evidence_items.fact: OpenAlex field proxy for cloud data warehouse query optimization/lakehouse/Iceberg returned 6 works in 2021 and 52 in 2025.
evidence_items.location: OpenAlex API meta.count by publication-year filter
evidence_items.limitations: Search-query proxy, not a curated bibliometric corpus.

evidence_items.fact: OpenAlex field proxy for enterprise AI data cloud/semantic layer/text-to-SQL returned 85 works in 2021 and 366 in 2025.
evidence_items.location: OpenAlex API meta.count by publication-year filter
evidence_items.limitations: Search-query proxy and not Snowflake-authored publication count.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake's foundational elastic data warehouse paper was accepted at SIGMOD 2016 and documents the shared-data cloud architecture.
evidence_items.limitations: Older foundational paper; current innovation must be judged with newer product and patent evidence.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake launched Arctic, an Apache 2.0 enterprise-grade LLM family with disclosed MoE architecture and training research details.
evidence_items.limitations: Arctic is important but not enough alone to define Snowflake as a frontier model company.

evidence_items.fact: iDIYAS reported Snowflake patent grants by year: 2021 157, 2022 218, 2023 214, 2024 201, 2025 152; 2026 partial count 44.
evidence_items.limitations: Patent grant documents, not simple families; 2025 may still be incomplete relative to final publication indexing.

evidence_items.fact: US11675780B2 covers partition-based scanning of external tables for query processing and lists US, CN, EP, KR, and WO family members.
US10942925 covers database query processing using a pruning index over micro-partitions.
iDIYAS reported 1,047 Snowflake patents, 2,271 forward citations, 25 EPO patents, and 3 Canadian patents.
evidence_items.limitations: Aggregator source; not a patent-office family census.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake disclosed that its architecture runs across three major public clouds and 53 regional deployments.
evidence_items.limitations: Regional deployment count does not reveal workload-level utilization.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake disclosed Snowpark for Java/Scala, Python support, Snowpark Container Services, Snowflake Intelligence, and Snowflake Postgres as productized platform capabilities.
evidence_items.limitations: Not every product capability has separate adoption metrics.

evidence_items.fact: R&D expense rose from $466.9 million in FY2022 to $1.969 billion in FY2026; capex rose from $16.2 million to $101.6 million.
evidence_items.limitations: R&D is company-wide and includes stock-based compensation.

evidence_items.fact: Cortex AI Functions became generally available in November 2025, adding production-ready AI functions inside the Snowflake SQL engine.
evidence_items.limitations: GA status does not disclose revenue contribution.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake reported 13,328 total customers, 790 Forbes Global 2000 customers, 733 customers with more than $1 million trailing 12-month product revenue, and 125% net revenue retention as of January 31, 2026.
evidence_items.limitations: NRR declined from 133% in FY2024 to 125% in FY2026.

evidence_items.fact: Product revenue increased from $2.667 billion in FY2024 to $4.472 billion in FY2026, and RPO reached $9.772 billion in FY2026.
evidence_items.limitations: Consumption model means timing of revenue recognition remains variable.

evidence_items.fact: Project SnowWork launched in research preview for a limited set of customers in March 2026.
evidence_items.limitations: Research preview is early adoption, not broad GA adoption.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake cited enterprises including Capita, Logitech, Telenav, United Rentals, and Wolfspeed using Snowflake Intelligence/Cortex Code-related AI capabilities.
evidence_items.limitations: Named-customer evidence does not quantify usage or revenue.

evidence_items.fact: Snowflake discloses risks around AI Technology development and use, customer adoption of AI features, data governance, security, privacy, and reliance on public cloud infrastructure.
evidence_items.location: FY2026 10-K forward-looking statements and risk factors

evidence_items.fact: Apache Iceberg provides an open table-format ecosystem that supports Snowflake's Polaris interoperability strategy.
evidence_items.limitations: Open standards reduce lock-in concerns but also lower switching barriers.

evidence_items.fact: Operating cash flow increased from $110.2 million in FY2022 to $1.222 billion in FY2026, while GAAP operating loss remained negative at $1.435 billion in FY2026.
evidence_items.limitations: Strong cash flow coexists with persistent GAAP operating losses.

layers.label: Science
layers.summary: The research base behind Snowflake's core platform is strong and has broadened into enterprise AI, semantic layers, text-to-SQL, open table formats, and governed AI functions.
layers.strong: Publication proxies rose sharply, and Snowflake has credible company-authored research assets including the SIGMOD warehouse architecture paper and Arctic model release.
layers.missing: Snowflake does not publish a complete current citation dashboard for Cortex, Snowflake Intelligence, or Project SnowWork.

normalization.rationale: Both field proxies exceed the 35% annualized-growth cap, so the growth metric is capped at 1.0.
Quality evidence is strong but not fully measured with a complete citation map.
Research topics map directly to generally available or deployed Snowflake capabilities.

layers.label: IP
layers.summary: Snowflake has a deep and technically specific patent base, but grant counts are no longer rising from the 2022-2024 peak.
layers.strong: Patents cover query optimization, pruning indexes, external-table scans, hybrid tables, replication, data sharing, LLM search, and hallucination safeguards.
layers.missing: A clean global simple-family time series and patent-to-paper citation map were not available from primary patent-office APIs in this run.

normalization.rationale: Absolute patenting is large, but the five-year grant trend falls from 2022-2024 levels into 2025.
Representative patents are implementation-specific and tied to Snowflake's database architecture.

metrics.label: Science to patent or assignee quality

normalization.rationale: Assignee quality and technical portfolio depth are high, even though source coverage is not a full family map.

layers.label: Industrialization
layers.summary: Snowflake shows strong industrialization: it has productized data, AI, container, open-catalog, and application capabilities across a large multi-cloud deployment base.
layers.strong: FY2026 10-K evidence shows 53 regional deployments across three major public clouds, productized Snowpark/Snowpark Container Services, Cortex AI GA functions, and heavy R&D investment.
layers.missing: Snowflake does not disclose detailed per-product utilization for Cortex, Intelligence, Postgres, SnowWork, or Polaris.

normalization.rationale: The technologies are productionized across a mature cloud platform rather than only announced.
R&D scale and capex growth are strong, but this remains a software/cloud platform rather than a capital-intensive manufacturing story.
Large live customer base and revenue scale provide a real learning surface for data and AI platform operations.

layers.label: Adoption
layers.summary: Adoption is very strong for the core AI Data Cloud and increasingly visible for AI products, though some 2026 agentic products remain preview-stage.
layers.strong: FY2026 metrics include 13,328 customers, 790 Forbes Global 2000 customers, 733 customers above $1 million trailing product revenue, 125% NRR, $4.472 billion product revenue, and $9.772 billion RPO.
layers.missing: Per-product revenue and utilization for Cortex AI, Snowflake Intelligence, Cortex Code, SnowWork, and Polaris are not separately disclosed.

normalization.rationale: Revenue and committed-performance evidence are large and growing.
Customer breadth spans broad enterprise usage and named AI customers.
Consumption expansion is proven, but some newer AI workflows remain preview-stage.

layers.label: Policy & Economics
layers.summary: The policy/economics layer is supportive but not clean: cash generation is strong, standards alignment is improving, but GAAP operating losses and AI/data-governance risks remain material.
layers.strong: Operating cash flow reached $1.222 billion in FY2026, and Polaris/Apache Iceberg strategy improves interoperability positioning.
layers.missing: Snowflake still depends on hyperscale cloud suppliers and faces unresolved privacy, AI governance, security, consumption variability, and GAAP profitability questions.

normalization.rationale: Governance architecture is strategically aligned, but regulation and data-risk exposure remain significant.
Open-catalog strategy helps ecosystem fit, but public cloud dependence is a real bottleneck and concentration risk.
Cash generation and revenue scale are strong, but persistent GAAP operating losses prevent a higher economic-readiness score.

normalization_notes.reason: Five-year field publication growth is more informative than one-year counts.
Open data provided grant counts, not fully normalized family counts; trend direction and absolute portfolio size were both considered.
Cloud software scale is nonlinear and better represented with log-like judgment.
Cash flow and GAAP operating loss point in opposite directions and require explicit judgment.
